spec_citations.spec_ref: miniplan Tests table (empty-repo onboarding) + external-plan-review.md R2-5/R2-6 ACCEPTED + spec 'zero testable-but-untested'
spec_citations.divergence: No test exercised the commitless/no_base onboarding path, and nothing proved the claim that makes Step H's skip load-bearing: that --verify-commit REJECTS a base-less commit. The promised amend then re-verify branch was likewise absent, while the ledger asserted zero testable-but-untested.

Step 1a writes the stamp to the WORKTREE, but Step H prescribed a bare git commit (index-only) and no step in the adopt skill ever staged anything - confirmed by grep across skill, references and scripts. Staging before 1a, the natural reading, ships pre-stamp blobs. The integration test invented a pathspec add and claimed it was exactly as the skill prescribes, which was false.

The cited test could not fail. Substring 'not' matches Nothing, cannot and Do not commit elsewhere in the same file, so the assertion reduced to 'the word continuous appears somewhere' and an inverted banner reading refreshed continuously passed it.

spec_citations.spec_ref: Ledger row 13 (restore does not clear unrelated work)
spec_citations.divergence: The cited test passed when --restore did nothing at all (the tree was already dirty from the drifted evidence file) and also when it DELETED the unrelated file, since a staged-then-deleted path still appears in porcelain. It could not detect the failure its own message named.

spec_citations.spec_ref: Ledger row 17 (Step H stamps before committing)
spec_citations.divergence: The cited test asserted only that the stamp anchor precedes the verify anchor. Moving the stamp instruction to after the commit step kept it green, so the before-committing half - the whole reason for placing it at Step H - was unpinned.

spec_citations.spec_ref: miniplan 'Verified against preflight_pr in an integration test' + external-plan-review R2-1 ACCEPTED
spec_citations.divergence: preflight_pr is never imported or called by any test in the diff; the delivered test asserts git status instead. The substitution is defensible but was undeclared, unlike the module-split deviation which was recorded.

spec_citations.spec_ref: miniplan (shortfall is FATAL, justified solely for a document with no Source-State line) + AC-2 principle that onboarding still finishes
spec_citations.divergence: An ABSENT evidence document was folded into the same fatal partial branch as a bannerless one and aborted onboarding, with a detail that misstated the cause - 'carries no Source-State banner' said of a file that is not there. Both sibling deliveries presence-filter instead, and Step F's seeder is documented non-blocking.

spec_citations.spec_ref: Ledger row 3 (abbreviated base stamped as the resolved full id)
spec_citations.divergence: The banner never carries the full id - banner_line truncates to 12 - and the cited test asserted the JSON report field rather than the document, so the row's claim was false as written and unproven where it mattered.

spec_citations.spec_ref: Ledger row 6 (this mode never resolves HEAD)
spec_citations.divergence: The guard patched the resolver module only. The CLI's own rev-parse HEAD goes through its own module reference and was unpatched, so the early-return guarantee asserted in the code comments was not pinned.
